blocks.text: 1. Dot-Product Attention

blocks.alt: A query and key go through a dot product to produce a score

blocks.text: Query, Key, and Value, the previous topic, formalized the three roles underlying Attention. Dot-Product Attention is the simplest concrete way to actually compute relevance scores, explored throughout this topic.
It works by using the genuinely straightforward dot product between Query and Key vectors, a genuinely simple, direct mathematical operation covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Scoring Step

This connects back to the scoring step, already covered in Query, Key, and Value. The Query genuinely gets compared against every Key to produce relevance scores, already covered there in only general terms.
This topic genuinely specifies exactly how that comparison actually gets computed, giving that earlier general description a genuinely concrete, mathematical form.
3. What A Dot Product Genuinely Measures

blocks.alt: A dot product measures similarity between query and key

blocks.text: A genuinely important mathematical recap connects back to vector operations, already covered implicitly throughout Backpropagation & Optimization. A dot product genuinely measures how genuinely aligned two vectors are.
This is a genuinely foundational mathematical fact that Dot-Product Attention directly exploits, using vector alignment as a genuinely natural proxy for relevance between the Query and each Key.

blocks.text: 4. Computing The Score

blocks.alt: A query vector and key vector multiply and sum to produce a score

blocks.text: The genuinely core computation connects back to the Query and Key, both already covered in the previous topic. Take the dot product of the Query vector with each individual Key vector, one at a time.
This genuinely direct, simple operation, already covered in this section, is repeated once per encoder position, producing exactly one relevance score for every single Key.
5. Interpreting A Higher Score

blocks.alt: A higher score means more relevant while a lower score means less relevant

blocks.text: This connects back to what a dot product measures, already covered in this topic. A genuinely higher dot product score means the Query and that Key are genuinely more aligned.

This directly translates into a genuinely higher relevance score for that specific encoder position, giving the eventual attention weights, already covered in Encoder-Decoder Attention, a genuinely intuitive mathematical basis.
6. The Simplicity Benefit

blocks.alt: Dot-product attention is compared against the more complex additive attention

blocks.text: This connects forward to Additive Attention, covered in the very next topic. Dot-Product Attention genuinely requires no additional learned parameters beyond the Query, Key, and Value projections themselves.
This is a genuinely important simplicity advantage explored further in direct contrast with the next topic, which introduces a genuinely different, more complex scoring approach.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This lack of additional parameters, already covered in this topic, is a genuinely important practical advantage, since it keeps the total parameter count lower than approaches requiring their own dedicated scoring network.

blocks.text: 7. A Genuine Computational Efficiency

This connects back to matrix multiplication's own computational efficiency, already covered generally throughout this course. Dot products genuinely map extremely efficiently onto modern hardware, already covered generally in Mixed Precision Training.

This is a genuinely real, practical reason this approach became so widely adopted, since Graphics Processing Units, already covered there, are specifically optimized for exactly this kind of matrix operation.
8. A Preview Of A Scale Sensitivity Issue

blocks.alt: A large dimension leads to large dot product scores

blocks.text: A genuinely important, honest limitation connects back to genuinely large vector dimensions, a real, practical consideration. Dot products can genuinely grow very large when vectors have many dimensions.
This is covered further in the very next topic of this module, which directly addresses exactly this genuine limitation with a genuinely simple, targeted fix.

blocks.text: 9. Recapping Turning Scores Into Weights

This connects back to turning scores into weights, already covered in Encoder-Decoder Attention. These genuinely raw dot product scores still genuinely need Softmax, already covered there, to become proper attention weights.
Dot-Product Attention genuinely only handles the scoring step, not the final normalization, a genuinely important scope clarification worth stating explicitly in this topic.
10. Recognizing When Dot-Product Attention Is Genuinely A Strong Choice

blocks.alt: Needing simple, fast scoring points toward dot-product attention

blocks.text: This connects back to wanting genuinely computational efficiency, already covered in this topic. Dot-Product Attention, already covered, directly delivers exactly that through simple, hardware-friendly operations.

This connects forward to Scaled Dot-Product Attention, covered in the very next topic, addressing this topic's own scale limitation. Understanding this simpler version first, already covered, is a genuinely necessary foundation.
11. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates computing Dot-Product Attention scores and observing how vector alignment affects the resulting relevance scores, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

query = np.array([1.0, 0.5, -0.3, 0.8])  # already covered as the Query in the previous topic

keys = np.array([
    [1.0, 0.5, -0.3, 0.8],   # genuinely identical direction to the query
    [-1.0, -0.5, 0.3, -0.8],  # genuinely opposite direction
    [0.1, 0.05, -0.03, 0.08], # genuinely same direction, smaller magnitude
    [0.5, -1.2, 0.9, 0.1],    # genuinely unrelated direction
])

# already covered as computing the score in this topic
scores = np.array([np.dot(query, key) for key in keys])
print("Dot-product scores (already covered in this topic):")
for i, score in enumerate(scores):
    print(f"  Key {i}: score = {score:.3f}")

print(f"\nHighest score: Key {np.argmax(scores)}, already covered as interpreting a higher score in this topic")
print("Notice the identical-direction key scores highest, and the opposite-direction key scores lowest")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the identically aligned Key scoring highest and the oppositely aligned Key scoring lowest, exactly the interpretation already covered in this topic: greater alignment directly means greater relevance.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Dot-Product Attention computes relevance scores using the dot product of Query and Key vectors.
A dot product measures how aligned two vectors are.
The Query gets compared to each Key individually, one dot product per Key.
A higher dot product score means greater alignment, translating to higher relevance.
It requires no additional learned parameters beyond the Query, Key, and Value projections.
Dot products map extremely efficiently onto modern hardware.
Dot products can grow very large when vectors have many dimensions.
The resulting raw scores still need Softmax to become proper attention weights.
Next up: Scaled Dot-Product Attention, directly addressing this topic's own scale sensitivity issue.
